events.text: At a ferry landing a stranger steps off the boat, {npc}, and the world goes very quiet. You have never seen {him} before. You know the way {he} will push the hair from {his} eyes a moment before {he} does it. {He} stops too, and frowns, as if {he} has forgotten a word that was on the tip of {his} tongue.

choices.text: Say hello, as if you have done it a thousand times

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You talk until the last boat has gone. Neither of you can say why it is so easy. By the end of the evening it feels as if you have only been apart a little while.

choices.text: Walk with {him} as far as the town, and keep {him} safe

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You walk {npc} to the town gate and make sure the road is safe. {He} thanks you, puzzled, and you watch {him} go in. It is enough that {he} is well.

choices.text: Let {him} pass. That life is over

effects.log: You stand aside and let {npc} walk past. Something in your chest that has been clenched for a very long time lets go. You wish {him} a whole life, without you in it.

events.text: A young traveller asks you the way to the next town, {npc}, and laughs at your directions in a way that stops your heart. You have heard that laugh before, from a small face, a long time ago, in a life that is not this one.

choices.text: Walk {him} there yourself, and talk all the way

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You walk {npc} all the way to the next town and you talk about everything. At the gate {he} says, "It is strange. I feel as if you have been looking out for me all my life."

choices.text: Give {him} your warmest coat and a safer road

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You send {npc} by the long road, the safe one, with your own coat. {He} will never know why a stranger cared so much. {He} does not need to.

choices.text: Point the way, and watch {him} go

effects.log: You point the way and watch {npc} walk off into a life of {his} own. You raised {him} once. This time {he} does not need you, and that is the best ending there is.

events.text: An old acquaintance of the town, {npc}, scolds you for not wearing enough in the cold, and then stops, embarrassed. "Forgive me," {he} says. "I do not know why I said that. You reminded me of someone." You know exactly who.

choices.text: Laugh, and let {him} scold you all the way home

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: {npc} scolds you all the way to your door, and you let {him}. It is the warmest you have been in years. After that {he} brings you soup when you are ill.

choices.text: Make sure {he} wants for nothing this winter

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You see to it quietly that {npc} has wood and rice all winter. Once, long ago, {he} did the same for you, and never said so either.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and let the old debt rest

effects.log: You thank {npc} and walk on. Whatever you owed {him} in that other life, you have carried it far enough. You set it down at the corner of the street.

events.text: In a teahouse a stranger, {npc}, corrects the way you hold your cup without thinking, two fingers here, the thumb there, exactly as a master once taught you in another life. {He} blinks at {his} own hand. "Now why did I do that?"

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you more

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You ask, and {npc} shows you, and shows you, and by nightfall the two of you are sparring in the yard behind the teahouse, laughing like old friends. Some lessons are not finished in one life.

choices.text: Stay near, and see that nobody troubles {him}

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You keep an eye on {npc} from then on. Once you drive off a pair of thugs before {he} even knows they were there. A teacher should be repaid, even across lives.

choices.text: Bow to {him}, once, the old way, and leave

effects.log: You bow to {npc}, deeply, the way a disciple bows, and walk out before {he} can ask why. Whatever was left to say between you is said.

events.text: A young fighter, {npc}, is practising forms on a riverbank, and every form has the same small fault you once spent a whole life correcting in a disciple of your own. You know, before you know how you know, exactly what {he} will get wrong next.

choices.text: Correct the fault, gently, as you always did

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, tries it your way, and gets it right on the first try. "How did you know?" {he} asks. You only smile. You teach {him} again, from the beginning.

choices.text: Teach {him} the one thing that will keep {him} alive

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You show {npc} a single guard, the one that would have saved a disciple of yours in another life. {He} learns it well. That is all you came to give.

choices.text: Watch for a while, and let {him} find {his} own road

effects.log: You sit on the bank and watch {npc} get it wrong, and then a little less wrong. {He} will find the way on {his} own this time. You leave before {he} looks up.

events.text: Someone bumps into you in a crowded market, {npc}, and catches your arm before you fall, and for a moment the two of you stand there gripping each other's wrists like two people who once swore an oath under a peach tree. Neither lets go first.

choices.text: Laugh, and buy {him} a drink

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: One drink becomes ten. By dawn you and {npc} are trading stories as if you had known each other all your lives, and swearing you will meet again. You will.

choices.text: Walk {him} home through the bad streets

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You walk {npc} home through the worst streets of the town, close at {his} shoulder. Nobody troubles you. At the door {he} grips your wrist once more, puzzled, and goes in.

choices.text: Let go first, and walk on

effects.log: You let go first. {npc} looks after you for a long moment, frowning, and then the crowd closes. An oath kept for a lifetime may rest.

events.text: A stranger at the next table, {npc}, finishes your sentence for you, the punchline of a joke you have told only once, to one person, in a life long over. Both of you go quiet. {He} looks as startled as you feel.

choices.text: Tell {him} the rest of the story

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You tell {npc} the whole story, and {he} laughs in all the right places, as if {he} had heard it before. By the end of the night you are friends again. Some friendships do not wait for memory.

choices.text: Pay for {his} meal and keep an eye on {him}

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You pay for {npc}'s meal before {he} can stop you, and keep an eye on {him} in the years after. {He} never quite works out why the stranger at the teahouse is so kind.

choices.text: Smile, and let {him} keep {his} own life

effects.log: You smile, finish your tea, and go. {npc} will have new friends in this life, and so will you. The joke was a good one, though.

events.text: You remember this sky. The red star has hung low all spring, and tonight it is brighter than the moon. In another life you were standing on this road when it fell. You know the very hour.

choices.text: Take the long road over the hills, now

effects.log: You walk all night over the hills. Near dawn the light comes down behind you, very fast and very quiet, on the road where you would have been. You walk on. Heaven wrote it; you did not read it the same way twice.

choices.text: Warn the village and lead everyone out

effects.log: Nobody believes you until you start carrying the children out yourself. When the red star falls on the empty square, the whole village is on the hill watching. They will tell the story for a hundred years.

events.text: You remember this sky. The river is black and high and the frogs have gone silent. In another life the water came over the dyke tonight and took the house with everyone asleep in it.

choices.text: Climb to the high temple before dark

effects.log: You sit on the temple steps all night listening to the river. At midnight it comes over the dyke, roaring, and takes the empty street. In the morning the sun comes up on you, alive.

choices.text: Wake the street and lead them uphill

effects.log: You hammer on every door. Some curse you; all of them follow. When the black water takes the street, the whole street is on the hill behind you, wet and cold and alive.

events.text: You remember this sky. All autumn the mountain above the pass has groaned at night. In another life it came down at dusk on the pass, and you were on it.

choices.text: Take the long road round the mountain

effects.log: The long road costs ten days and 10 taels for the ferry. At dusk on the fourth day you hear the pass go, far behind you, like a door slammed in another world.

choices.text: Turn the caravans back at the foot of the pass

effects.log: You stand in the road and turn the carts back, one after another, while the drivers shout at you. At dusk the mountain turns over in its sleep. Nobody shouts after that.

events.text: You remember this sky. The grey birds have come in from the south, and the physicians are boiling their knives. In another life the grey fever took you in three days.

choices.text: Go north at once, with clean water and bitter roots

effects.log: You leave before the first cough in the town and live a whole winter on the high road with boiled water and bitter roots. The fever never finds you.

choices.text: Teach the town what you remember of the cure

effects.log: You remember what the physicians learned too late, last time. You teach them now. You catch a little of the fever yourself, and so does the town, and almost all of you live.

events.text: You remember this sky. For a month there has been thunder out of a clear sky, every afternoon a little closer. In another life it stopped being far away, and that was the end.

choices.text: Go down into the old mine and wait

effects.log: You sit in the dark of the old mine for three days, listening to the dry thunder walk past overhead. When you climb out, the sky is only a sky.

choices.text: Sit in the open and meditate on it

effects.log: You sit under the clear sky and let the thunder come. It strikes the tree beside you, and the hair on your arms stands up for a week. You understand something about lightning that you did not before.

events.text: You remember this sky. The festival lanterns are burning blue tonight, and nobody can say why. In another life someone stepped out of the crowd behind you, and you never saw the face.

choices.text: Stay home with the door barred

effects.log: You bar the door and sit up with a lamp until dawn. In the morning they find a stranger asleep in your doorway with a knife in hand and no memory of why.

choices.text: Go to the festival and keep your back to a wall

effects.log: You walk the festival with your back to every wall. When the stranger steps out of the crowd you are already turning. The knife goes into the lantern pole. The face, at last, is just a face.

events.text: A red star hangs low over the road all spring, and the old people stop talking when they look at it. Every night it seems to look at you. You cannot shake the feeling that it is waiting for you to be somewhere.

choices.text: Leave the region before the year turns

effects.log: You pack and take the road out of the province, travelling by night under the red star. It follows you the whole way. Every road looks like the same road.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until the sign has passed

effects.log: You shut yourself in a cave under the hill to sit out the year, far from any road. Through the mouth of the cave the red star looks smaller every night, as if it has lost sight of you.

choices.text: Consult a fortune teller about the sign

effects.log: The fortune teller squints at the star and talks for an hour about wealth and a long, lucky road. You pay 5 taels and walk home along the road under the red star, no wiser.

events.text: The river runs black and high all summer, and the frogs fall silent at dusk. You dream of water under the door, and wake each morning with cold feet.

choices.text: Leave the region before the year turns

effects.log: You sell what you cannot carry and move to the dry hills two provinces away, where the nearest river is a creek. It costs 10 taels. The black river is somebody else's river now.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until the sign has passed

effects.log: You bar the door of your house by the river and sit in seclusion through the high water, breathing slowly. The frogs stay silent. The river goes on rising.

choices.text: Consult a fortune teller about the sign

effects.log: The fortune teller says the water means money coming. You pay 5 taels. Walking home along the dyke, you notice how high the river is, and how black.

events.text: All autumn the mountain above the pass groans at night, like an old man turning in his sleep. Your road goes over that pass more often than any other.

choices.text: Leave the region before the year turns

effects.log: You set out at once for the next province. The only road out goes over the pass. You cross it in a hurry, and the mountain groans above you all the way.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until the sign has passed

effects.log: You find a quiet cave on the mountain itself and sit in seclusion there. At night the stone around you groans, very close, and you tell yourself it is only the wind.

choices.text: Consult a fortune teller about the sign

effects.log: The old fortune teller does not look at your palm. She looks at your boots. "Not the road," she says. "The mountain. Do not be under it at dusk this coming year, whatever the reason." You pay 5 taels and believe her.

events.text: Grey birds fly in from the south as the winter comes, and the physicians start boiling their knives. You catch yourself counting the birds on the roof.

choices.text: Leave the region before the year turns

effects.log: You go north before the birds have finished arriving, with clean water and a sack of bitter roots, and take lodgings in a cold mountain town where no bird lands. It costs 10 taels.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until the sign has passed

effects.log: You shut yourself in your room in the town to sit out the winter in seclusion. Through the shutters you can hear the grey birds on the roof, and in the street the first coughing.

choices.text: Consult a fortune teller about the sign

effects.log: The fortune teller tells you to wear red and avoid the number four. You pay 5 taels. The grey birds are still on every roof when you come out.

events.text: For a month there is thunder out of a clear sky, every afternoon, always a little closer. The dogs hide under the beds. You find yourself looking up a great deal.

choices.text: Leave the region before the year turns

effects.log: You take the open road to the next province, under a clear sky. Every afternoon the thunder comes after you, a little closer, as if it knows the way.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until the sign has passed

effects.log: You go down into the deep cellar of an old shrine and sit in seclusion there, under stone and earth. Overhead the dry thunder rolls, and down here it sounds very far away.

choices.text: Consult a fortune teller about the sign

effects.log: The fortune teller says thunder from a clear sky is a sign of promotion. You pay 5 taels and walk home under the clear sky, listening.

events.text: The lanterns burn blue at the year's festival, and nobody can say why. For days afterwards you feel eyes on your back in every crowd, and turn round to find no one.

choices.text: Leave the region before the year turns

effects.log: You leave for another city. The feeling of eyes on your back comes with you, in every inn and on every road.

choices.text: Go into seclusion until the sign has passed

effects.log: You shut yourself away in seclusion in a hut outside the town. At night you hear someone walk round it, slowly, once, and then go away.

choices.text: Consult a fortune teller about the sign

effects.log: The fortune teller turns over a card and goes pale. She describes a face, a scar through one eyebrow, a limp. "Next year, on the night of the blue lanterns," she says. You pay 5 taels, and now you know whom to watch for.

events.text: In a village where you have never been, an old woman spits at your feet. "Your face," she says. "A man with your face poisoned our well, long before you were born." You have never been here. Some part of you is not surprised.

choices.text: Dig them a new well, with your own hands

effects.log: It takes the whole season. When the water comes up clean the old woman brings you a cup of it, and does not spit. (Atonement)

choices.text: Walk on. It was not you

effects.log: You walk on. It was not you. The cup of water you did not drink stays with you for a long time.

events.text: A temple that keeps orphans is falling down, roof by roof. A monk looks at you a long while, as if reading something written on your forehead, and says, "You owe this place something. You do not know what. Neither do I."

choices.text: Pay for the roof and stay to mend it

effects.log: You pay 40 taels for the tiles and stay to lay them. The children call you uncle and aunt by turns and argue about which. (Atonement)

choices.text: Leave a coin and go

effects.log: You leave a coin in the bowl and go. The monk bows anyway, as if he knew you would.

events.text: On a hillside you find an untended grave whose name has worn away. You cannot stop looking at it. You are certain, in a way you cannot explain, that the one buried here died because of you, in a life you do not remember.

choices.text: Tend the grave, and come back every year

effects.log: You clear the weeds, set a new stone, and burn incense. You come back the next spring, and the next. Each time it is a little lighter. (Atonement)

choices.text: Turn away from it

effects.log: You turn away. The worn stone follows you into your dreams for a few nights, and then stops.

events.text: Two families in the town have hated each other for five generations, over something no one remembers. When you walk between them in the street, both sides go quiet and stare at you, as if you were the one who started it.

choices.text: Sit them down together, and do not leave until it ends

effects.log: It takes three days and a great deal of tea. In the end the two eldest shake hands, and both of them look at you as if a debt has been paid. (Atonement)

choices.text: It is not your quarrel

effects.log: You leave them to it. The quarrel goes on, the way old quarrels do.

events.text: A flood has carried off the only bridge, and the poor of the far bank cannot reach the market. Nobody will build a ferry for people with nothing to pay. You find you cannot sleep for thinking about it.

choices.text: Build a ferry, and pole it yourself

effects.log: You build a flat ferry from salvaged timber and pole it back and forth all season for nothing. Your shoulders ache. Something deeper aches less. (Atonement)

choices.text: Someone else will do it

effects.log: Someone else does, eventually. You hear about it in a teahouse and do not finish your tea.

events.text: A wounded stranger lies in the road, and everyone walks round. As you kneel, a voice in your head that is almost a memory says: you walked round once, too, in another life. Many times.

choices.text: Carry the stranger to a physician

effects.log: You carry the stranger three li to a physician and pay what is asked. The stranger lives. You never learn the name. You do not need to. (Atonement)

choices.text: Walk round, like everyone else

effects.log: You walk round. The voice in your head says nothing at all, which is worse.
